title: Provisioning: integration tests for state machine transitions (failure injection + rollback assertions)
author: Gabe Wilson
description: Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint, we now have a persisted provisioning state machine (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed) and stage executors that can retry and roll back. This PR adds integration tests that exercise the state machine end-to-end against a real DB, with deterministic failure injection and rollback assertions. The intent is to catch regressions where we (a) skip/duplicate transitions, (b) mark Ready early, (c) lose failure reasons, or (d) fail to execute rollbacks/cleanup callbacks when a stage fails mid-run. Summary of changes: Adds a provisioning integration test harness that boots a disposable Postgres schema, seeds a pool request, and runs the provisioner loop with stubbed stage executors. The executors can be configured per-stage to succeed, fail, or fail once then succeed (to validate retry behavior). The tests validate: 1) happy path transitions: Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready; 2) failure injection in Imaging: transitions to Failed with error classification, emits audit trail, and executes rollback hook for partially-applied artifacts; 3) failure injection in Bootstrapping with retry: stays in Bootstrapping on first failure (retryable), then proceeds and ultimately marks Ready; 4) non-retryable validation failure: transitions to Failed and does NOT advertise Ready to routing; 5) rollback/cancel behavior: ensure cleanup callbacks are invoked exactly once and run is marked terminal, and that a subsequent retry run starts from Requested with a new run_id but preserves prior run history for audit. Test plan: - Local: go test ./... -tags=integration -run TestProvisioningStateMachine; requires docker for postgres via testcontainers (see below). - CI: adds a dedicated Buildkite step that runs integration-tagged tests; the step is allowed to retry once on infrastructure flake (docker pull) but tests themselves are deterministic. Implementation notes: - Uses testcontainers-go to run Postgres and applies the same migration set as the provisioner service (ensures schema drift is caught). - Introduces a small testkit in controlplane/provisioning/testkit with a FakeExecutor that records invocations, supports per-stage fail patterns (always/once/never), and exposes a CleanupCalled() counter for rollback assertions. - Removes sleeps from state progression tests by wiring a deterministic clock + polling helper with max deadline; we assert on exact transitions stored in provisioning_runs and provisioning_run_events tables rather than relying on log output. - Adds coverage for failure reason shape: error_category, error_code, and user_facing_message are asserted to be set for terminal failures. Rollout/ops: No production behavior changes. This is test-only coverage to protect the state machine + rollback semantics during the staging/prod pilots. Follow-ups: - Add a concurrency test for two runs on the same pool_id (ensuring idempotency + lock behavior) once ENG-2742 follow-ups land on run locking semantics. - Expand failure injection to cover imaging timeouts on specific SKU/region once the fallback logic (ENG-2757) is merged.

tests: failure injection for Imaging and Bootstrapping (retry + terminal)
tests: assert rollback hooks and cleanup call counts
ci: add buildkite step for integration-tagged provisioning tests

review_conversation: Ethan Park (requested changes): These tests look great for transition coverage, but can we also assert that we emit provisioning_run_events for every stage start/finish? Right now the test only checks the final run state. Also: avoid time.Sleep; it’s been flaky in other integration tests. Gabe Wilson (author): Good call. Updated to assert stage start/finish events (and failure event) in provisioning_run_events with correlation_id present. Removed sleeps; replaced with waitForRunState polling helper + deterministic clock injection in the test harness. Rafael Mendes (comment): For rollback assertions, please verify cleanup executes exactly once (I’ve seen double-cleanup in retries). Also ensure a terminal Failed run never gets marked Ready even if a late stage completes. Gabe Wilson: Added CleanupCalled() counter assertions per stage executor; tests now assert cleanup count == 1. Also added a guard assertion that Ready is never set after a terminal failure event exists (regression test for the "late completion" bug). Miles Thornton (comment): Can we include at least one multi-region-ish scenario (different region in config) to ensure no region-specific branching breaks the event model? Not asking for a full concurrency test, but a second run with different region would be useful. Gabe Wilson: Added a second parametrized case that uses eu-west-1 and verifies the same transition/event invariants. Concurrency test is called out as follow-up once lock semantics settle. Benji Okafor (nit): README update should mention integration tag and docker requirement; also please pin testcontainers version in go.mod to avoid surprise upgrades. Gabe Wilson: README updated; testcontainers pinned and go.sum updated. Ethan Park (approval): LGTM after changes. Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Thanks for removing sleeps. Miles Thornton (approval): Looks good.
